children: A working paper written on 2026-11-16, published nearly as written. Local file paths, private repository names and personal names have been removed.
Purpose: ground the redesign of the map's layers panel in the data that exists. Sources read:
(Hamilton catalogue), the overlay run manifest a local working copy, and the pulls and tiles under a local working copy on deb. Nothing was pulled or changed for this note.
480 datasets are catalogued for the City of Hamilton. Reviewed: 228 not relevant, 106 context only, 27 unclear, 119 relevant (of which 23 are admitted to the control sheet and 7 curated).
55 control-sheet rows touch Hamilton or Ontario. All are marked
Licence clearance is recorded as "unclear" for 43 of the 55
; that column needs filling before a layer is shown (record the licence for provenance even where a hard rule already permits publication).
11 layers are already joined to all 166,745 parcels (the overlay run). Their facts are in the dossier today; none is drawn on the map.
Street basemap (OpenStreetMap via Protomaps, light and dark)

Tier 4: admitted to the control sheet, not yet pulled
Most relevant to industrial land and investment:
Hamilton railways; truck route network; trails; MTO controlled areas.

development applications; building and demolition permits (2008 to present); vacant building registry; city-owned properties; licence registers (salvage yards, public garages, trades); businesses by employee count.
existing land use primary blocks; Provincially Significant Employment Zones; older zoning (pre-rural).

wetlands (City and provincial); natural heritage system; areas of natural and scientific interest; wooded areas; provincial parks; subwatersheds; conservation authority areas; NPCA regulated floodplain; Conservation Halton regulation limit; contours.
wastewater and combined-sewer catchments with water pressure districts.
industrial land, rail corridors, brownfield and disused sites, industrial facilities.
Tier 5: catalogued as relevant, not yet admitted

Business improvement areas; community improvement project areas; heritage properties; environmentally sensitive areas; rural settlement areas; airport; landfills and transfer stations; air monitoring sites; cooling towers; real estate sales; growth targets; the "SiteSelector" service. Water and sewer network layers (mains, valves, nodes, lift stations) are catalogued but flagged
and should stay out until reviewed.
What stands between the data and the map
is singular) and the prepublish allowlist permits only
on parcel features. The allowlist already has entries for
, so more layers were anticipated; the manifest and layer catalogue need to carry several tilesets.
Each thematic layer needs a short allowlist (for zoning: the zone code; for land use: the class) and label register entries for its classes.
Fill the 43 "unclear" clearances for whatever is chosen.
Tier 2 is small except secondary plan land use and zoning; buildings is the heavy one (about 28 MB as tiles).
zoning, secondary plan land use, urban boundary, employment lands, Greenbelt, Niagara Escarpment Plan, conservation authority regulated areas (three sources shown as one group), parks.
Wave 2 (new pulls, high value for industrial readers):

railways, truck routes, Provincially Significant Employment Zones, development applications, building permits, vacant building registry, licensed salvage yards and garages, wetlands and natural heritage.
buildings, existing land use, infrastructure catchments, business counts, heritage, improvement areas.
The panel should be organised by theme, not as a flat list, and should be honest about state:
held (can be switched on once tiled)

. Proposed groups: Base map (style), Parcels, Planning, Protected and regulated, Movement, Activity on land, Built form, Environment. Each layer row needs its source, date and a legend; a layer with classes (zoning, land use) needs a class legend that can be filtered.
